Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a lightweight asks list so we can qualify performance and residency constraints for Skyline's prototype: 

1) Target latency SLOs: you mentioned 50–100 ms p95 for single-turn HL7-to-natural-language calls; can you confirm p50/p95 targets for streaming use-cases (real-time transcription + streaming tokens)?
2) Typical throughput: expected sustained requests/sec and peak burst concurrency (expected # of concurrent sessions during morning batch).
3) Payload characteristics: average and max prompt length (tokens), attachment sizes (if any), and whether requests include PHI (yes/no).
4) Regional constraints: primary region = us-west, with EU failover and APAC read-only. Confirm data residency constraints for patient data (does EU-bound data need to remain in-region at rest?).
5) Networking: will you be able to share traceroutes or egress IP allowlist requirements? We can provide our NAT ranges.

I attached a short SLO template (RWI_SLO_template_v2.xlsx) you can fill in; if you prefer, we can schedule a technical deep-dive with Karthik to align on batching/concurrency and streaming knobs.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Elaine: populate the SLO template with approximate numbers (latency p50/p95, RPS, concurrency) by EOD Monday.
- Marissa: I’ll loop you in for procurement/discussion on Reserved/Dedicated if numbers justify it.
- Karthik: please be ready to take a short call on Monday for any low-level questions.

If you'd rather, we can also start with a small pilot (2–3 endpoints) scoped for your worst-case daytime traffic to validate latency/p95 and streaming posture.

Thanks —
Vivek

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications inline and answers to the asks: 

1) Latency SLOs: for user-facing triage flows we want p50 ~ 30–40 ms and p95 < 120 ms (streaming target p95 < 200 ms for token emission). These are tight but reflect clinician expectations.
2) Throughput: baseline sustained ~ 25 rps, peak bursts up to 250 rps during morning rollouts. Concurrent sessions: roughly 300 concurrent streaming sessions during peak (each session sends small token batches).
3) Payloads: average prompt ~ 120 tokens; max during longer context rehydration ~ 10k tokens. Attachments are mostly PDFs (patient summaries) 0.5–2 MB. Data will include PHI; so residency and encryption-at-rest are critical.
4) Regional residency: All patient data processed for EU-based clinics must not leave EU at rest. Processing can route to EU instances for inference. For APAC clinics, initial compliance requires data to be routed to APAC region (we may accept a read-only copy in US for analytics but not the primary store).
5) Networking: James can share traceroutes and firewall rules early next week.

I'll fill the SLO template with these numbers and send it back by Monday EOD. We also want to see a brief note on expected unit cost estimates for hosted vs. dedicated for this traffic profile.

Thanks,
Elaine

Thanks all — quick technical readout before we schedule the dive: 

Summary recommendations (high level):
- Latency: Achievable p50 25–45 ms and p95 80–140 ms for single-turn requests on high-frequency small prompts on Dedicated A10-like pools with continuous batching disabled for low-latency paths. For streaming token emission p95 ~ up to 180–220 ms depending on sequence length and model.
- Throughput/Concurrency: For sustained 25 rps with 300 concurrent streaming sessions we recommend: 2 Dedicated instances (8 x A10-equivalent) with autoscale headroom for 3x burst handling. If quantized variants acceptable, 1 smaller pool + autoscale may suffice but expect p95 increases ~20–40 ms.
- Batching: Use adaptive micro-batching (0–10 ms wait) for text-gen calls; for streaming sessions set batching window near 0 to favor latency. Enable KV-cache warmup during session start for long-context rehydrations.
- Regional routing: Configure primary-region pinning for EU clinics (in-region inference + KMS). For failover, use synchronous fallback to US-only if acceptable for non-PHI workloads; for EU-PHI strict policy, no cross-region fallback. For APAC, recommend a read-only APAC edge for caching (not storing PHI) and active inference in APAC Dedicated if/when compliance requires.

Open questions for Skyline (please confirm):
- Will all PHI require in-region key management (customer KMS) or is host-managed KMS acceptable for EU?
- For long context (10k tokens), are you okay with a hybrid strategy where only a redacted index is sent to US for retrieval while full rehydration is in-region?

I can run a short validation run (2-hour window) against a synthetic load that mimics 250 rps bursts and 300 concurrent streams; that will produce latency histograms for p50/p95 and a cost estimate. If you share an example dataset (anonymized), I can include more realistic token distributions.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
